questions.text: In the last 7 days, on how many days did you eat breakfast?
questions.help: Anything substantial before your first lecture counts: bread, hoppers, string hoppers, oats, milk rice or a rice meal.

questions.text: On how many days did you eat 2 or more servings of vegetables?
questions.help: 1 serving = ½ cup of cooked vegetables or mallum (one cupped hand), or 1 cup of raw salad (one fist). Potatoes do not count.

questions.text: On how many days did you eat dark green leafy vegetables?
questions.help: Gotukola, mukunuwenna, kankun, spinach or kathurumurunga. 1 serving = ½ cup cooked or as mallum (one cupped hand).

questions.text: On how many days did you eat at least 1 serving of fruit?
questions.help: 1 serving = 1 medium fruit (banana, orange, guava) or ½ cup of cut fruit such as papaya, pineapple or mango (one cupped hand). Fruit juice does not count.

questions.text: On how many days did you eat pulses?
questions.help: Dhal (parippu), chickpeas (kadala), green gram, cowpea or soya meat. 1 serving = ½ cup cooked (one cupped hand).

questions.text: On how many days did you eat fish, eggs or chicken?
questions.help: 1 serving = 1 egg, or a piece of fish or chicken about the size of your palm.

questions.text: On how many days was your main starch a whole grain?
questions.help: Red or brown rice, kurakkan, atta flour roti or bread, or oats. 1 serving = 1 cup of cooked rice (one fist) or 1 roti.

questions.text: On how many days did you have milk, curd or yoghurt?
questions.help: 1 serving = 1 glass of milk (200 ml) or 1 small cup of curd or yoghurt (about 100 g).

questions.text: On how many days did you have sugary drinks or sweets?
questions.help: Soft drinks, sweet tea or coffee, packet juice, cake, chocolate, kavum or ice cream. 1 serving = 1 glass or small bottle (200 ml), or 1 piece of a sweet.

questions.text: On how many days did you eat short eats, fried food or fast food?
questions.help: Rolls, patties, cutlets, vadai, kottu, fried rice, instant noodles or burgers. 1 serving = 1 short eat or 1 plate.

questions.text: How often were your main meals balanced?
questions.help: A balanced meal has a starch (rice, roti or hoppers), vegetables and a protein (dhal, egg, fish, chicken or soya), like the healthy plate.
